description_short: A complete guided mettā bhāvanā practice led by Bhante Bodhidhamma, developing loving-kindness through systematic cultivation of goodwill toward all beings.
description_long:
This guided meditation session offers a comprehensive mettā bhāvanā (loving-kindness development) practice led by Bhante Bodhidhamma. The practice emphasizes that mettā is fundamentally about cultivating an attitude of goodwill rather than forcing pleasant emotions to arise—understanding that even when warm feelings don't immediately surface, the practice is still transformative.

The meditation follows a traditional structure, beginning with someone we regard warmly and progressively expanding outward: to near and dear ones, friends and colleagues, ourselves, our immediate surroundings, and eventually radiating to encompass all beings throughout the world. Both worldly blessings (health, prosperity, long life) and spiritual blessings (freedom from greed, hatred, fear, and delusion) are offered at each stage.

A significant portion of the practice addresses forgiveness work—first seeking forgiveness from those we have hurt, then offering forgiveness to those who have hurt us. Bhante guides practitioners to observe the emotional patterns that arise: self-righteousness, shame, hurt, and revenge, helping us recognize how clinging to these states causes our own suffering. The practice includes the four great efforts: developing what is beautiful, removing what is unwholesome, preventing future negativity, and cultivating undeveloped virtues.

The session incorporates the Karaṇīyamettā Sutta chanted in Pāli, connecting practitioners to this ancient teaching on loving-kindness. This practice serves as both a foundation for concentration and a powerful means of softening the heart, preparing the mind for deeper insight meditation.
